security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples, placeholder secrets, and TypeScript template literals in reference material. No prompt-injection attempt or hidden credential exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is the evaluation harness, which can launch user-selected local commands and forward user-supplied headers to remote MCP endpoints.

remediation.suggestion: Document that the evaluation harness should be run only against trusted MCP servers, and consider adding an explicit confirmation or command allowlist.
Warn users to send authorization headers only to trusted MCP endpoints and to use low-scope tokens during evaluation.
Prefer pinned documentation revisions or remind users to treat fetched documentation as untrusted reference material.

semantic_findings.title: User-Selected MCP Server Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness accepts a command and arguments from CLI options and passes them to stdio MCP connection setup. This is expected for testing, but users should only evaluate trusted local servers because the launched command runs with their privileges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command and arguments flow directly from CLI options into StdioServerParameters. The risk is controlled because there is no shell interpolation, but the spawned process still runs locally.

semantic_findings.title: User-Provided Remote Endpoint and Header Forwarding
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness accepts SSE or HTTP URLs and headers from CLI arguments and passes them to MCP client connections. This is expected for remote testing, but authorization headers can be sent to an untrusted endpoint if users choose one.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI options are passed into SSE and HTTP connection objects. The behavior is user-directed, so the risk depends on endpoint trust and token scope.

content.user_title: Build MCP Servers for API Integrations
content.value_statement: Building an MCP server requires protocol choices, validation, and evaluations that are easy to miss. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, implementation, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains agent-centered MCP tool design, naming, annotations, and response formats.
Guides Python FastMCP server setup with Pydantic validation, async requests, and error handling.
Guides Node and TypeScript MCP server setup with Zod schemas and SDK registration patterns.
Provides an evaluation workflow for creating XML question sets and checking answers.
Includes a Python harness for running evaluations against stdio, SSE, or HTTP MCP servers.
Covers pagination, truncation, rate limits, and actionable error messages.
limitations: It is a guide and harness, not a generator that guarantees production-ready server code.
Remote documentation links can change and should be reviewed before use.
The evaluation harness requires a valid Anthropic API key and may use paid API calls.
Security review of generated MCP servers remains the user responsibility.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API Connector
use_cases.description: Map user workflows to high-value MCP tools before writing server code.

use_cases.title: Implement a Typed MCP Server
use_cases.description: Follow Python or TypeScript patterns for validation, error handling, pagination, and transport setup.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Tool Quality
use_cases.description: Create read-only evaluation questions and run them against a local or remote MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First MCP Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one external service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-builder skill to plan an MCP server for [service]. Identify the core workflows, proposed tools, required authentication, and response formats.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Python Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python guidance in mcp-builder to outline a FastMCP server for [service]. Include Pydantic models, async API helpers, pagination, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a TypeScript Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the TypeScript guidance in mcp-builder to design an MCP server for [service]. Include tool registration, Zod schemas, shared API utilities, and build steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder to create a read-only evaluation plan for my MCP server. Include ten realistic questions, answer verification steps, and quality risks to inspect.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output_examples.output: A workflow-based tool list, authentication notes, pagination strategy, and evaluation ideas for read-only project and task questions.

output_examples.input: Review my Python MCP server design.
output_examples.output: Feedback on input validation, async API access, error messages, response size controls, and missing evaluation coverage.

output_examples.input: Prepare evaluation questions for a GitHub-style MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of stable, read-only question themes with expected answer verification guidance and report review steps.

best_practices: Start with user workflows and choose tools that complete full tasks.
Validate every input with Pydantic or Zod before calling external services.
Run read-only evaluations before adding write or destructive operations.
anti_patterns: Wrapping every REST endpoint as a separate tool without workflow design.
Returning unbounded API payloads that overwhelm the model context.
Testing long-running stdio servers directly without timeouts or an evaluation harness.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build MCP servers that expose external APIs to AI tools through structured, validated tools.

faq.question: Does it support Python and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Python FastMCP and Node or TypeScript MCP SDK implementations.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning, implementation, testing, and review, but the user still creates and verifies the server.

faq.question: Can it test remote MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. The included harness supports stdio, SSE, and HTTP transports for evaluation runs.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The evaluation harness needs an Anthropic API key. Target service credentials depend on the MCP server being tested.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production security review?
faq.answer: It provides security-minded guidance, but production servers still need separate review, least-privilege credentials, and operational monitoring.
